newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AIF, Infratil in winning Perth airport bid.
newsitem.headline: AIF, Infratil in winning Perth airport bid.

text.p: The Australian Infrastructure (AIF) Group said on Wednesday it had a 10 percent stake in the winning A$643 million bid for the government-owned Perth airport through the Australian Airport Property Fund.

It said Infratil Australia Trust has a 49 percent stake in the consortium known as the Airstralia Development Group, while Airports Group International had 16 percent and the Australian Airport Property Fund had 35 percent.
Airports Group International Ltd is a subsidiary of Lockheed Martin Corp.

The Australian Airport Property Fund is managed by infrastructure investor Hastings Funds Mangement Ltd and is owned by AIF, the Utilities Trust of Australia, the Emergency Services Superannuation Scheme and the Development Australia Fund.

The Perth airport sale was announced earlier on Wednesday alongside the sale of Melbourne Airport to Australian Pacific Airports Corp, a consortium of BAA Plc and the Australian Mutual Provident (AMP), and the sale of Brisbane to a consortium including the Dutch government-owned Schiphol airport and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Hastings Funds Management Managing Director Michael Fitzpatrick said in a statement that the investment would be funded using the group's existing cash reserves.
AIF said Perth airport has enjoyed a period of sustained growth in traffic volumes, handing 4.4 millions and about 89,000 traffic movements in 1995/96.
The three airports were sold for A$3.3 billion.
